title: Platform systems & services: playbook, runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and retrospective
author: Aisha Thompson
body:
Summary:
This consolidated playbook captures the current systems-and-services map for the Platform team, standard how-tos for dashboards/alerts, canonical runbooks for high-severity incidents, a short retrospective template and the near-term roadmap. Use this page as the single source of truth for oncall runbooks, dashboard ownership, SLOs, and planned platform work for the next two quarters.

1) Purpose and scope
- Audience: Platform engineers, SREs, infra owners, oncall rotations, and product partners.
- Scope: cluster control plane, routing layers, logging/metrics stack, core platform services (auth-proxy, routing-gateway, build-broker, cron-workers), and our Grafana/Prometheus observability surface.

2) Systems & services inventory (owner, criticality, SLO)
| Service | Owner | Criticality | Target SLO | Alert contact |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| routing-gateway | eng-platform/networking | high | availability 99.95% | #platform-oncall |
| model-proxy (edge) | eng-platform/runtime | high | p99 latency < 500ms | #runtime-oncall |
| build-broker | eng-platform/ci | medium | job success >= 99% | #ci-oncall |
| auth-proxy | eng-platform/security | high | auth failures < 0.1% | #security-oncall |
| logging-ingest | eng-platform/observability | medium | ingestion lag < 30s | #observability |

3) Standard how-tos: dashboards, alerts, and ownership
A. Dashboard creation checklist (Grafana)
- Create dashboard in team folder /dashboards/platform. Name: <service>-overview.
- Panels: error-rate, request-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, request concurrency, KV-cache hit ratio.
- Add README panel (markdown) describing owner, data sources, dashboard refresh, and runbook link.
- Assign owner in the dashboard JSON metadata and tag with labels: "platform", "service:<service-name>".
- Link to the runbook (internal URL) and to the alert rules that drive the panels.
- Verify with oncall: at least one oncall must confirm visibility and access.

Example Grafana panel query (Prometheus):
- p95 latency (service): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="routing-gateway"}[5m])) by (le))

B. Alert rule template (Prometheus Alertmanager)
- Alert name: <SERVICE>_HighErrorRate
- Expr: sum by(job) (rate(http_requests_total{job="<service>", status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum by(job) (rate(http_requests_total{job="<service>"}[5m])) > 0.005
- For: 5m
- Severity: critical (pager) if > 0.5% sustained for 5m, warning (slack) if > 0.2% for 10m.
- Annotations: summary, runbook_url, playbook_steps.
- Routing: critical -> #platform-pager, warning -> #platform-alerts.

C. Ownership and SLA mapping
- Every dashboard and alert must have an owner (team alias) and a documented oncall escalation path.
- Owners must review alerts quarterly and remove noisy rules or tune thresholds.

4) Runbooks (canonical templates and one full example)
A. Runbook template (for all services)
- Detection: alert name, PromQL, dashboard panels to inspect.
- Triage checklist: severity, blast radius, affected customers, impacted SLO.
- Mitigation steps (ordered): temporary mitigation -> target remediation -> long-term fix.
- Communication: status page, slack channels, paging list, incident lead.
- Post-incident: timeline, RCA, action items, owner assignments.

B. Example: routing-gateway - High 5xx rate (Critical)
Detection
1. Alert: routing-gateway_HighErrorRate fires (5m).
2. Oncall sees increase in 5xx on /v1/generate endpoint and dashboard spike in p95 latency.

Triage (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm scope: kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=routing-gateway; check pod restarts and OOMs.
2. Check rolling deploys: gitlab pipelines and recent deploys (last 30m).
   - CLI: gitlab-ci status, or check /pipelines on internal CI.
3. Check logs: 
   - kubectl logs -n platform <pod> --since=15m | grep -i error
4. Check downstream dependencies: model-proxy upstream, auth-proxy responses.

Mitigation (10-30 minutes)
1. If CPU spikes: scale routing-gateway horizontally: kubectl scale deploy/routing-gateway --replicas=<N+2>.
2. If specific pod OOM: increase memory limit for pod (create immediate canary) and rollback erroneous config.
3. If upstream failure: fail open to fallback model variant and re-route traffic (see emergency routing playbook).

Communication
- Post status to #platform-incident with summary, estimated ETA, and mitigation step.
- If customer-facing impact > 10% of requests or SLO breach: update status.redwood.ai with incident summary.

Recovery and follow-up
- When error rate returns to baseline for 30 minutes, begin controlled rollback/test changes in staging and schedule postmortem.
- Postmortem template: timeline, contributing factors, detection, remediation, preventative actions (owner + due date).

5) Retrospective template and recent notes
- Template: incident title, incident lead, timeline, what went well, what went wrong, action items (owner + due date).
- Recent retro summary (Q2 2026):
  - Issue: noisy default alerts caused multiple P2 escalations.
  - Action items: centralize alert ownership (assigned), reduce duplicate alerts by 60%, create alert-sanity-runbook. Owners: Miguel Rivera (alert cleanup) due 2026-08-01.
  - Result: reduced paged incidents from noise by 45% in subsequent 6 weeks.

6) Roadmap (next 6 months)
- Q3 2026 (owner):
  - Observability modernization: migrate to unified metric naming and tag schema (eng-platform/observability) — target completion 2026-09-30.
  - Auto-tuning alert thresholds using baseline detection (ML) — research spike 2 weeks (eng-platform/sre).
  - Dashboard templating: ship SDK for consistent JSON exports and CI validation (eng-platform/infra).
- Q4 2026 (owner):
  - Canary routing service: per-customer canary capabilities for Dedicated customers (eng-platform/runtime).
  - Platform cost dashboard and per-route token accounting (finance + eng-platform).

7) Oncall, escalation and contact info
- Primary oncall: platform-pager rotation (1-week), secondary backup: platform-backup.
- Pager escalation: primary -> 15m -> secondary -> 30m -> eng lead.
- Slack channels: #platform-incident (incidents), #platform-alerts (low-sev), #platform-oncall.
- Pagerduty schedule: Platform-Oncall (link in internal PD).

8) Operational runbooks and playbooks (links)
- Emergency routing: /confluence/eng-platform/emergency-routing-playbook (internal).
- Grafana dashboard standards: /confluence/eng-platform/grafana-standards.
- Onprem deployment runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/onprem-deploy-runbook.json

9) Metrics, SLOs and error budget policy
- Standard SLOs: availability 99.95% (monthly), p95 latency targets per-service (see inventory table).
- Error budget burn policy: if burn rate > 2x for 1 week -> hold non-critical deploys and convene triage working group.

10) CI validation and ownership checklist (pre-merge checks for dashboard/alert PRs)
- PR must include: dashboard JSON (validated by grafana-lint), alert rule test (promtool check), owner field, runbook link, and QA sign-off from oncall.

11) Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- kubectl (check pods): kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=<service> -o wide
- tail logs: kubectl logs -n platform <pod> --follow --since=1h
- scale deployment: kubectl scale deploy/<name> --replicas=<n>
- promtool check rules: promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yaml
- Grafana export: grafana-cli dashboard export <uid> > dashboard.json

Change log:
- 2026-07-15: created (Aisha Thompson)
- 2026-08-02: added alert threshold tuning guidance and PromQL examples (Miguel Rivera)
- 2026-09-08: updated roadmap Q4 and added retrospective summary (Katerina Ivanov)
